text:
Hector: morning check-in on the onboarding sweep for kestrel-ptq-v2. We see a weird cluster: model sometimes emits a top-level array of actions, sometimes a single object, and occasionally wraps JSON inside a markdown code fence. Parser expects a single object. Current parse failure ~1.9%.

Sam: can you paste a couple raw hits (no redaction)?

Hector: pasted two different ones the harness logged:
```
```json
[
  {
    \"action\": \"open_ticket\",
    \"params\": {\"title\": \"Login error\"}
  },
  {
    \"action\": \"notify\",
    \"params\": {\"channels\": [\"#ops\"]}
  }
]
```
and
```
```
{
  \"action\": \"search\",
  \"params\": {\"q\": \"pricing page\", \"max\": 3}
}
Some notes: found three results.
```
```
Notice the fence and the trailing natural language in the second sample.

Jo: hmm. New sanitizer rules we talked about should cover both: 1) if output is an array, accept first element if it validates; 2) strip fenced blocks. But we need to detect intentional multi-action semantics (customers may actually want batching).

Sam: agree. We should treat array->first-element as sanitizer only in the canary; log full-array examples for product to evaluate. If array length >1 and the actions are different, mark as \"multi-action-candidate\" and sample for UX.

infra-bot: queued job: \"kestrel-ptq-parse-harness-12k\" ETA ~50m :hourglass_flowing_sand:

Jo: also observed a small subset where the model emits HTML-escaped braces like `{` which our extractor misses. Add a pre-pass to unescape common HTML entities before JSON extraction.

Sam: add another axis: decoder biasing on punctuation. For ptq variants we've seen more escapes; try logit-scale punishment on tokens matching backtick, `<`, `>`, and also boost for `{` and `}`. Run a tiny 1k probe to validate no regression in legitimate prose.

Hector: experimental plan: three branches over 12k calls: A = baseline, B = sanitizer pre-pass (unescape + strip fences + array->first-if-valid), C = B + punctuation logit-scaling + one retry (temp=0.0) if parse still fails. Metrics: parse pass rate, semantic match, fraction of arrays that are actually intended multi-action, false-accepts, p50/p95 latency, tokens delta. We'll also surface up to 300 sampled multi-action arrays for PM review.

Jo: please also capture kvcache length and whether the prompt included system instruction about response format. That might correlate.

Sam: I'll instrument the small probe and add a flag to the harness for the logit-scale setting.

eval-bot: test job started: run-id=run-20260323-kestrel-ptq-12k :rocket:

Hector: timeline: results + example dump + proposed PR for sanitizer by tomorrow morning. If B reduces parse failures to <0.4% with <0.15% false-accepts we'll propose enabling as runtime fallback behind a config toggle.

Jo: thanks, team. Ping me if you need help labeling the multi-action UX samples. :mag:
